import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Integrality and supercongruences of the factorial ratio $\frac{(6n)! n!}{(3n)! (2n)!^2}$

Integral factorial ratio sequence:
$$a(n) = \frac{(30n)! n!}{(15n)! (10n)! (6n)!}$$

*References:*
- [A211417](https://oeis.org/A211417)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA211417


/--
Integral factorial ratio sequence:
$$a(n) = \frac{(30n)! n!}{(15n)! (10n)! (6n)!}$$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Nat.factorial (30 * n) * Nat.factorial n) /
  (Nat.factorial (15 * n) * Nat.factorial (10 * n) * Nat.factorial (6 * n))

open Nat Int Finset

def coprimeIndices (r : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.range (r + 1)).filter (fun i => 1 ≤ i ∧ Nat.gcd i 30 = 1)

/--
The product term in the denominator of the general conjecture:
$$\prod_{i = 1..r, i \text{ coprime to } 30} (30n - i)$$
We define this in ℤ to handle the $n=0$ case where $30n-i$ in the product might be negative.
-/
def divisorProduct (n r : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  (coprimeIndices r).prod (fun i : ℕ => 30 * (n : ℤ) - (i : ℤ))


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 77636318760 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 53837289804317953893960 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 43880754270176401422739454033276880 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 38113558705192522309151157825210540422513019720 := by rfl


/--
It appears that $a(n)/(30n - 1)$ is integral for all $n$ (checked up to $n = 1000$). - _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/211417.wip.lean#L243"]
theorem thirty_mul_sub_one_dvd_a (n : ℕ) : (30 * (n : ℤ) - 1) ∣ (a n : ℤ) := by
    sorry

/--
Conjecture: "7*a(n)/(2*n + 1) ... [is an] integer for all n (checked up to n = 1000)."
- _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a211417/blob/cad1fb228b5b80573cab3eeb92c8be57fd73c506/lean/OeisA211417FC.lean#L866-L868"]
theorem seven_mul_a_dvd_two_mul_add_one (n : ℕ) :
    (2 * (n : ℤ) + 1) ∣ 7 * (a n : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture: "a(n)/(3*n + 1) ... [is an] integer for all n (checked up to n = 1000)."
- _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a211417/blob/cad1fb228b5b80573cab3eeb92c8be57fd73c506/lean/OeisA211417FC.lean#L1173-L1175"]
theorem a_dvd_three_mul_add_one (n : ℕ) :
    (3 * (n : ℤ) + 1) ∣ (a n : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture: "a(n)/(5*n + 1) ... [is an] integer for all n (checked up to n = 1000)."
- _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a211417/blob/cad1fb228b5b80573cab3eeb92c8be57fd73c506/lean/OeisA211417FC.lean#L1446-L1448"]
theorem a_dvd_five_mul_add_one (n : ℕ) :
    (5 * (n : ℤ) + 1) ∣ (a n : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture: "42*a(n)/((2*n + 1)*(3*n + 1)*(5*n + 1)) [is an] integer for all n
(checked up to n = 1000)." - _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a211417/blob/cad1fb228b5b80573cab3eeb92c8be57fd73c506/lean/OeisA211417FC.lean#L1514-L1524"]
theorem forty_two_mul_a_dvd_product (n : ℕ) :
    ((2 * (n : ℤ) + 1) * (3 * (n : ℤ) + 1) * (5 * (n : ℤ) + 1)) ∣
      42 * (a n : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture: "More generally, for r >= 1, we conjecture that there exists a constant D(r) such that
D(r)*a(n)/Product_{i = 1..r, i coprime to 30} (30*n - i) is integral for all n."
- _Peter Bala_, Aug 28 2025

This generalizes `thirty_mul_sub_one_dvd_a` (the $r = 1$ case where $D(1) = 1$).

**Proof sketch** (kernel-checked development at the `formal_proof` permalink below, which
proves the non-vacuous form with the explicit positive witness $D = (r!)^{r^2}$):
Legendre-valuation analysis of the Landau step function
$\Delta(x) = \lfloor 30x \rfloor + \lfloor x \rfloor - \lfloor 15x \rfloor -
\lfloor 10x \rfloor - \lfloor 6x \rfloor$, whose values lie in $\{0, 1\}$. Three
ingredients: a unit-class rigidity lemma ($\Delta_c = 1$ for every unit class $c$ modulo
$30$), a witness-uniqueness bound for prime powers $p^k > r$ (at most one factor of the
divisor product is divisible by $p^k$), and a uniform low-layer budget for $p^k \le r$
absorbed by the witness constant.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/chy4pro/formal-conjectures/blob/fbc6706451b0e80787580d91ee6c252c121e0165/FormalConjectures/OEIS/211417.lean#L651"]
theorem general_divisibility (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) :
    ∃ D : ℤ, 0 < D ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, (divisorProduct n r) ∣ (D * (a n : ℤ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Supercongruence: "a(p^k) == a(p^(k-1)) ( mod p^(3*k) ) for any prime p >= 5 and any positive
integer k." - _Peter Bala_, Jan 24 2020

More generally, "the congruences a(n*p^k) == a(n*p^(k-1)) ( mod p^(3*k) ) may hold for any
prime p >= 5 and any positive integers n and k."
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem supercongruence (p k : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp5 : 5 ≤ p) (hk : 0 < k) :
    (p : ℤ) ^ (3 * k) ∣ ((a (p ^ k) : ℤ) - (a (p ^ (k - 1)) : ℤ)) := by
  sorry

end OeisA211417

findings.description: The module title at line 20 gives the factorial ratio (6n)! n! / ((3n)! (2n)!^2), whereas both OEIS A211417 and `OeisA211417.a` use (30n)! n! / ((15n)! (10n)! (6n)!). These are different sequences: at n = 1 the title's ratio is 30, while a(1) = 77636318760. The definitions and theorem statements use the correct sequence; only the title is wrong.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A211417's %N line states `a(n) = (30*n)!*n!/((15*n)!*(10*n)!*(6*n)!).` Read through the official data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A211/A211417.seq. Peter Bala's integrality proof at https://oeis.org/A211417/a211417_1.txt uses the same formula.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the fraction in the module title with `(30n)! n! / ((15n)! (10n)! (6n)!)`. Leave `a` unchanged.

status_issues.source_status: OEIS presents this prime-power case as a known congruence with a proof reference in Peter Bala's comment dated January 24, 2020. Only the subsequent, more general arbitrary-multiplier statement is phrased tentatively.
status_issues.evidence: The current A211417 comment states the exact congruence and adds: 'write a(n) as C(30*n,15*n)*C(15*n,5*n)/C(6*n,n) and use equation 39 in Mestrovic, p. 12'. Equation (39) in https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.3057 gives binom(u p^k,v p^k) ≡ binom(u p^(k−1),v p^(k−1)) modulo p^(3k). Apply it to (u,v)=(30,15),(15,5),(6,1). The denominator binomial is congruent to 6 modulo p, hence invertible for every prime p≥5, so cancellation proves precisely the Lean statement. OEIS text was read at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A211/A211417.seq.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research solved` and include OEIS's binomial-congruence proof reference in the docstring. The mathematical statement need not change.

reformulations.difference: Lean defines the sequence using natural-number division, rather than a rational factorial quotient.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The denominator is positive and divides the numerator for every n ≥ 0. Bala's cited proof establishes this using Legendre's formula and the floor inequality floor(15x) + floor(10x) + floor(6x) ≤ floor(30x) + floor(x). Thus natural division is exact. In `/workspace/review/KitaKen1-check.lean`, I proved the exact equality between `(a n : ℚ)` and the source's rational quotient, and an associated ↔, using the cited development's checked denominator-divisibility theorem. The resulting proofs have no sorryAx dependency.

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses integrality as integer divisibility and explicitly takes the positive clearing constant D in ℤ; OEIS simply says a constant D(r) > 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every factor 30n−i is nonzero: equality to zero would make i a multiple of 30, contradicting gcd(i,30)=1. Consequently quotient integrality is equivalent to the stated divisibility. Restricting the clearing constant to integers loses nothing: at n=0, a(0)=1, so the source condition gives D/divisorProduct(0,r)=z for an integer z, forcing D=z·divisorProduct(0,r) to be an integer. The rational-quotient ↔ and product nonvanishing were proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, without sorryAx.

review.notes: Checked all 15 declarations. The five initial-value lemmas match the official b-file. Lean computations verified factorial exactness and all five fixed divisibility claims for 0≤n≤100, the supercongruence for p∈{5,7,11,13} and k∈{1,2}, and the proposed general witness for 0≤n,r≤20. All six cited solved divisibility claims were supported by kernel-checked proofs; two scratch copies needed only import/API compatibility updates. In particular, the general-divisibility artifact contains the positive-witness theorem `OeisA211417.general_divisibility_strong` at line 555. The normal OEIS pages were Cloudflare-blocked, but its official data mirror supplied the full entry. No mathematical statement or definition defects were found, and the target file was not modified.
